questions.question_text: Do you think Poppet & Pine Toys Ltd should keep the certified plastic and introduce continuous improvement teams rather than switch to the cheaper supplier? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Keeping the certified plastic withstands the 1.5 metre drop test reliably [k], with under 1% failure versus 4% for the cheaper material [app], protecting child safety and the national toy retailer's approval [an]. However, the cheaper supplier would save $21,600 a year [k], tempting for a business only 4 years old with 12,000 toys made monthly [app], though failures in the 4-month retailer audit could end the account [an]. scenario_stem:
Seacliff Fish & Grill is a family-run fish and chip restaurant in a coastal town in Country X, operating for 16 years with 9 employees. Monthly revenue is $48,000, and the lunch rush averages 120 covers between 12:00 and 14:00. Average wait times reached 18 minutes, and 15% of the 400 monthly online reviews mention cold food or order mistakes.

The owners must choose between two options to fix this. Option one is hiring 2 extra kitchen staff for the lunch rush at $1,600 each per month. Option two is a $12,000 kitchen redesign plus quality training for all 9 staff, building a total quality management culture with daily checklists and customer feedback cards. Either change must be in place before the summer tourist season.

questions.question_text: Define 'quality'.
questions.model_answer: Quality is how well a product or service meets customer needs and expectations, for example fitness for purpose and consistent standards [2].

questions.model_answer: Reason 1: Good quality food and accurate, prompt service raise customer satisfaction [k], encouraging repeat visits during the 120-cover lunch rush [app]. Reason 2: Positive reviews attract passing trade [k], countering the 15% of 400 monthly reviews mentioning cold food or order mistakes [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Seacliff Fish & Grill of adopting total quality management in the kitchen.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Total quality management makes all 9 staff responsible for quality [k], so daily checklists catch order mistakes before plates reach tables [app], cutting the 18-minute average wait [an]. Benefit 2: Total quality management builds a culture of continuous feedback and improvement [k], using customer feedback cards to refine service each week [app], lifting review scores above current levels [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think Seacliff Fish & Grill should hire 2 extra kitchen staff at $1,600 each per month rather than invest $12,000 in a kitchen redesign and quality training? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Hiring 2 extra kitchen staff adds kitchen capacity immediately [k], directly cutting the 18-minute wait during the 120-cover lunch rush [app], which should reduce the 15% of reviews mentioning cold food [an]. However, the extra wages cost $1,600 each per month, about $38,400 a year forever [k], whereas the $12,000 redesign plus quality training builds lasting habits across all 9 staff [app], tackling the root causes of errors, not just symptoms [an]. Overall, the $12,000 redesign and training is the stronger investment because it fixes processes and motivates staff rather than adding permanent wage costs [eval], provided the owners can fund $12,000 before the summer tourist season [eval].
